description: Agent Cybersecurity: submit a component and patch record with its patch policy: the policy with the days allowed to patch a critical, high, medium and low vulnerability and its text; each component in the inventory with its id, name, version, the day it reaches end of life and whether the record flags it end of life; each known-vulnerability match as recorded with its id, the component it names, its severity (critical, high, medium or low), the day it was published, its status (open, patched, mitigated or accepted), the day it was patched, and for an accepted risk who accepted it and until when; and optionally the day the record is read on. The signed report gives the patch window for each severity, the inventory with the components versioned, every match with its severity, the days from publication to the patch or to the day read on, its window and its state as within, overdue, patched late, closed, accepted or off the inventory, and the end-of-life components with those unflagged, and counts them, and names an overdue record: a critical or high vulnerability open past its patch window and a component past end of life that the record does not flag; then a medium or low vulnerability open past its window, a patch applied after the window, a risk acceptance with no owner or end or one that has ended, a flagged end-of-life component still in the inventory and a vulnerability naming a component missing from the inventory, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No inventory, a component with no version, no vulnerability matches, no window for a severity present, a match with no severity or publication day, or no day read on for an open match leaves the record unverified. This reads the component and patch record: wever_breach-path-check reads where work goes when it hits a limit, the escalation and the stop, not a security breach or the patches applied, and wever_security-disclosure-check reads a vulnerability disclosure policy or security.txt file, not the components patched. Verdict cyber_patch_overdue, cyber_patch_partial, cyber_patch_unverified or cyber_patch_current. POST /api/cyber-patch-check. Reads the security records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment, system scan, probe or external write. Agent Cybersecurity reads an organization’s own security records after the fact and checks them against the stated policy and against themselves: standing access, the secrets inventory, the component and patch record, the exported configuration, logging coverage, backup and restore evidence, a vendor’s security evidence and incident readiness. Beside it, the Agent Risk checks such as wever_risk-exposure-check read one planned action’s worst case and limits before it runs, while a cyber check reads security posture from the records; and the security reads elsewhere in the catalog keep their families, each named beside the check it meets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-cybersecurity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-cybersecurity/.

as_of.description: The day the records are read on, such as 2026-11-02.

eol_flagged.description: Whether the record flags it end of life.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

critical_days.description: Days allowed to patch a critical vulnerability.
